newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares close slightly weaker but off lows.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares close slightly weaker but off lows.

text.p: * NZ shares close off their lows
* Telecom ends off low but may not have bottomed yet
* Mkt depressed by short term corporate earnings prospects
Price movements at close
LAST CHG
334 +9 * NZSC cap index -7.09 at 5,109.31
375 +7 * Volume NZ$62 million. Futures -3 at 1,175
701 -5 * Other movers - -35 -15
New Zealand shares ended a touch weaker on Friday but off their lows as Telecom recouped some of its losses towards the close.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index ended 2.07 points lower at 2,328.29, with Telecom down six cents at NZ$7.00.
The index had been off 12 points and Telecom had dipped as low as $6.96 before recovering some of the lost ground.
"The market's finding it very hard to regain its feet. It's been a really difficult week for the market," said Cavill White's Don Turkington.
The index has shed 58 points this week while Telecom has fallen 37 cents. "Telecom's been the dictating stock all week," Turkington said.
He said there appeared to be some support for Telecom at $7.00, but the market generally did not appear to have any reason to rally in the short term.
"I think we've go to see particulay the (90-day) bank bill rate come off significantly before we'll get a resumption in life here.

"We've got a market that seems to be fascinated by rather poor short term profit prospects and not yet with enough confidence to look beyond for some pick-up in the economy at the end of this year," Turkington said.
"We're just stuck in a rut."
However, Lion Nathan continued its strong run, rising seven cents to $3.75, and Carter Holt Harvey gained nine cents to $3.34, although brokers noted it was still down three cents for the week.
